summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Tobacco smoke contains Nicotine (adrenal stimulant raising BP/HR), Carbon Monoxide (binds hemoglobin causing hypoxia), and polycyclic aromatic carcinogens causing oral/lung/bladder cancer. Chronic alcohol abuse progresses from fatty liver to irreversible Cirrhosis. Abrupt cessation of addictive substances produces physical Withdrawal Syndrome.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ADDICTION PATHOPHYSIOLOGY & WITHDRAWAL
                         
   Tobacco (Nicotine) ──► Adrenal Medulla ──► Adrenaline/Noradrenaline (↑ BP & HR)
   Tobacco Smoke      ──► Carbon Monoxide (CO) ──► Carboxyhemoglobin ──► Tissue Hypoxia
   Alcohol (Ethanol)  ──► Acetaldehyde ──► Fatty Liver ──► Cirrhosis of Liver
   Abrupt Cessation   ──► Physical Withdrawal Syndrome (Tremors, Anxiety, Sweating, Seizures)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 10.1 Pathophysiology of Tobacco Smoking
- **Nicotine**: An alkaloid that stimulates the **Adrenal Gland Medulla** to release **Adrenaline (Epinephrine)** and **Noradrenaline (Norepinephrine)** into blood circulation $\longrightarrow$ causes peripheral vasoconstriction, elevated blood pressure, and tachycardia.
- **Carbon Monoxide ($\text{CO}$)**: Binds hemoglobin with $200\times$ higher affinity than oxygen, forming **Carboxyhemoglobin** ($HbCO$), reducing the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood and causing chronic tissue hypoxia.
- **Carcinogenicity**: High concentrations of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (**3,4-Benzopyrene**, tar) dramatically increase the risk of cancers of the **lung, oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, esophagus, and urinary bladder**, as well as coronary heart disease and emphysema.

### 10.2 Alcohol Metabolism & Hepatic Pathology
- **Metabolic Pathway**: Ethyl alcohol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) is oxidized in the liver by **Alcohol Dehydrogenase (ADH)** into **Acetaldehyde** (a highly toxic intermediate), which is further metabolized by **Aldehyde Dehydrogenase (ALDH)** into acetate.
- **Hepatic Consequences**:
  1. *Fatty Liver Syndrome (Steatosis)*: Excessive $\text{NADH}$ production inhibits beta-oxidation of fatty acids, accumulating intracellular lipid droplets in hepatocytes.
  2. *Alcoholic Hepatitis*: Acute inflammation and necrosis of liver parenchyma.
  3. *Cirrhosis of the Liver*: Irreversible deposition of fibrous scar tissue, nodular regeneration, portal hypertension, and liver failure.

### 10.3 Psychological & Physical Addiction
- **Dependence & Tolerance**: Receptors down-regulate, requiring progressively higher doses to achieve the initial euphoric effect.
- **Withdrawal Syndrome**: Sudden cessation after prolonged use unleashes acute autonomic hyperactivity characterized by **tremors, profuse sweating, extreme anxiety, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, and grand mal seizures**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Wernicke-Korsakoff Syndrome
conceptBreakdown.title: Wernicke-Korsakoff Syndrome
conceptBreakdown.content: Chronic alcoholism causes severe Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency, leading to Wernicke's encephalopathy (confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia) and Korsakoff's psychosis (anterograde amnesia and confabulation).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Fetal Alcohol Syndrome (FAS)
conceptBreakdown.title: Fetal Alcohol Syndrome (FAS)
conceptBreakdown.content: Maternal alcohol consumption during pregnancy readily crosses the placenta, causing Fetal Alcohol Syndrome characterized by microcephaly, facial dysmorphism, intellectual disability, and congenital heart defects.
